[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
William Glasgow's birth before 1690 at Cavers is an estimate retained in the structured fields as uncertain. The identified marriage record does not state his age, birthplace or parents.

William “Glasgon” married [[Scott-69166|Margaret Scott]] at Hummelknows on 4 March 1708/09.<ref>FreeREG transcription, Cavers marriage register, William Glasgon and Margaret Scott, 4 March 1708/09, “Married in Hummelknows”; see also “Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910,” FamilySearch database, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYQG-3XD record XYQG-3XD].</ref> The structured date is entered as 4 March 1709, with Hummelknows retained together with the Cavers parish context.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1605]] is assessed at 29% (uncertain). Inherited uncertain Polwarth father Glasgow-1605; William's 1708/9 Hummelknows marriage names no parents. A 1658 Polwarth father could have an adult son marrying in 1709, and the inherited route places the groom in a compatible Borders generation. The marriage itself supplies no parent or origin.

Uncertain paternity; the documented Cavers adult William-4138 is a possible earlier identity for the groom, not proof that the Polwarth child was his father.

Next useful test: Compare the groom’s family and Cavers adult records for a named relative or age.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-3587 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-3587]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


The attached [[Glasgow-1605|William Glasgow]] is retained only as an uncertain father. The marriage record names no parents.

[[Glasgow-4138|William Glasgow]], a Cavers/Ormistoun servant documented in 1679–84, is a possible earlier identity for this 1708/09 groom. The earlier records and this marriage are compatible in locality and chronology, but neither identifies the groom by age, occupation or relative; they do not yet prove one man. The attached Glasgow-1605 father is a separate, unproved Polwarth baptism hypothesis.<ref>Findmypast, Scottish Covenanters 1679–1688, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPR%2FCOVENANT%2F028558&tab=this 1679 Cavers deposition] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPR%2FCOVENANT%2F028560&tab=this 1684 Ormistoun servant list].</ref>

An Isabel Glasgon, daughter of a William and of Humble Knows, was baptised on 27 August 1710.<ref>FreeREG transcription, baptism of Isabel Glasgon, 27 August 1710, father William, abode Humble Knows; mother not named.</ref> She is a strong candidate child of William and Margaret because of the name, date and place, but the record does not name her mother. She should not be attached as their proved child without corroboration.
